title: CIA 'psychic spy' claimed to see ancient city on Mars - decades later others say they saw the same apocalyptic end
excerpt: CIA 'psychic spy' claimed to see ancient city on Mars - decades later others say they saw the same apocalyptic end
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

22/09/2026 20:19

In May 1984, one of the people involved in the CIA's experiments with so-called "remote viewing" claimed to have seen, through psychic perception, the end of an ancient civilization on Mars.

Today, decades later, other people who claim to have had similar experiences say they saw almost identical scenes: large cities, unusual inhabitants, and a catastrophe that destroys everything.

These accounts remain paranormal claims and there is no scientific evidence proving that people can see distant places through "remote viewing" or that such a civilization existed on Mars.

However, the story continues to attract attention, especially because of its connection to a real American intelligence program during the Cold War.

A witness claims to have seen the end of Martian civilization

A person who only gave the name "Brady" told the Daily Mail that he claims to be able to perform "astral projection," a paranormal concept according to which a person's consciousness can leave the body and travel to other places.

Brady claims that during one such experience he found himself on Mars, but not on today's desert planet.

According to him, he saw an inhabited Mars in the very distant past.

He described the experience as "heartbreaking and dramatic", claiming that a giant blue wave destroyed civilization.

"Everyone suddenly panicked. Most were looking up, others were running. Screams and panic could be heard echoing between the buildings," he said.

Brady claims that he then saw an extremely large celestial body approaching the planet.

"It was circular, extremely large. I felt a mixture of despair and acceptance of fate," he said.

According to his account, the earth began to tremble and a colossal wave appeared on the horizon, swallowing everything in front of it.

A story reminiscent of the CIA experiment of 1984

Brady's description has attracted attention because of its similarities to the claims of Joseph McMoneagle, one of the most well-known people who participated in American "remote viewing" experiments.

During the 1970s and 1980s, American intelligence agencies and the military experimented with people who claimed they could perceive information about distant places, objects, or people without physically seeing them.

These experiments were conducted as part of programs that later became known as "Project Stargate".

The main goal was to understand whether such capabilities could have military or intelligence use, particularly against the Soviet Union.

McMoneagle became one of the program's most popular figures.

Unusual task: "Visit Mars a million years ago"

In a 1984 experiment, McMoneagle took on an extremely unusual target.

The experiment document stated:

"Planet Mars. Time of interest: approximately one million years BC."

McMoneagle later said that he did not know in advance what target he was trying to perceive.

Following coordinates provided by officials, he claimed to have "visited" the Cydonia Mensae area on Mars, a region made famous by the photograph called "Face on Mars," taken by the Viking probe.

In the now declassified report, McMoneagle described what he thought was a large pyramidal structure.

"I see a pyramid shape. It's very tall. It looks like it's in a large low area. It has a yellow, ochre color," his transcript says.

"Very tall and thin people"

When asked to "move back in time," McMoneagle claimed to see inhabitants of a disappearing civilization.

"I'm seeing... like a shadow of people, very tall, very thin. It's just a shadow. It's like they were there, but now they're not," he declared during the experiment.

He described pyramidal structures, canyons, obelisks, dust storms, and an atmosphere that, in his perception, was being destroyed.

McMoneagle interpreted the footage as signs that the inhabitants of Mars were facing a catastrophe and might have attempted to flee to another world.

Again, these statements do not constitute scientific evidence for the existence of an ancient Martian civilization.

Brady claims the city resembled Dubai

Decades after McMoneagle's experiment, Brady says he repeatedly tried to replicate his experience.

He even described this as a kind of obsession, saying that at one point he thought almost exclusively about returning to the vision of Mars.

According to him, the city he saw was modern and magnificent.

"It was a bit like Dubai, but the atmosphere and setting felt like a summer day in England," he said.

He claims the area was bustling with life.

"It was full of people, very active and lively. Everyone was about 1.80 to 2.10 meters tall, very thin, with pale skin, white on blue."

Another researcher claimed to have seen a civilization on Mars.

Brady is not the only one to have made such claims.

Courtney Brown, associate professor of political science at Emory University and author of the books "Cosmic Voyage" and "Cosmic Explorers," has written about his experiments with "remote viewing" of Mars.

Brown claimed to have also seen the Cydonia region and an ancient Martian civilization.

According to his description, the inhabitants had large eyes and delicate bone structure.

He claimed that their society had been struck by a great catastrophe.

"At its peak, Martian society was technologically comparable to ancient Egypt. They lived in harsh conditions, but they could feed their families, live in cities, and participate in community life. Then a great catastrophe occurred, and many Martians died," Brown wrote.

He also speculated that some of them might have survived and drifted to other areas of the solar system.

There is no astronomical or archaeological evidence to support these claims.

Why does McMoneagle remain such a controversial figure?

The interest in McMoneagle is not only related to his vision for Mars.

One of the most famous episodes in his career is related to a 1979 experiment, when he was asked to describe a Soviet object.

McMoneagle claimed to have perceived a large building near the White Sea in the north of the Soviet Union.

He described an unknown type of submarine, with sloping missile tubes and an unusual double structure.

At the time, the description was met with skepticism.

It was later confirmed that the Soviet Union was building a new class of ballistic submarines, known as the Typhoon class, which was made public in the early 1980s.

Supporters of "remote viewing" use this case as an example of successful prediction.

Skeptics, however, argue that such cases do not prove paranormal abilities, as historical "remote viewing" experiments have not produced consistent and reproducible evidence by scientific standards.

Ancient Mars continues to fuel the imagination

Modern science has proven that Mars in the past had flowing water, lakes, and much wetter conditions than today.

However, so far no confirmed evidence of cities, artificial structures or an intelligent civilization has been found on the red planet.

It is this mix between what science knows about ancient Mars and unusual accounts like McMoneagle's that continues to fuel theories, books, and debates.

For now, the story of the "lost civilization of Mars" remains an intriguing tale related to an unusual chapter in American intelligence experiments - not a scientifically proven fact. /GazetaExpress/
